cells.value: No national farmer-specific digital-literacy rate is published for Egypt. Best available evidence (regional, single-source): IFPRI RCT baseline phone survey, Minya & Beni Suef governorates, Jul-Sep 2023, n=3,332 farmers: 52% cite their own digital illiteracy as a key obstacle to using mobile applications; 54% cite unawareness of digital apps; 49% cite lack of smartphone access; 72% own a smartphone (64% among smallholders); 33% have home internet data access. These are barrier-shares and access rates, not a direct digital-literacy rate - do not score against the H 10/25/50/75 thresholds without a construct decision.
cells.source_title: Abdelaziz, F. & Abay, K.A. (2025). Digital literacy training to promote diffusion of digital agricultural tools to smallholder farmers: Evidence from a randomized intervention in Egypt. IFPRI Discussion Paper 2359 (baseline survey Jul-Sep 2023)
cells.search_trail: Searched 2026-08-22 in tier order: T1 - MCIT/CAPMAS ICT Indicators bulletins and mcit.gov.eg/en/Indicators (household/individual-level ICT usage; rural smartphone ownership 68% of households 2021-22 per ICT Indicators Bulletin cited in IFPRI DP 2359; no farmer-disaggregated digital-skills series); no ITU or WDI farmer-specific skills series exists -> T2 - CGSpace/IFPRI: found IFPRI DP 2359 (RCT baseline, PDF read in full for sections 3.2-3.3) and its peer-reviewed version in Food Policy (ScienceDirect S0306919226000758); stopped per tier order.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE FROM PRIOR: prior desk pass recorded '~46-48% face awareness/literacy barriers'; the actual published figures are 52% (farmer digital illiteracy) and 54% (unawareness of apps) - prior numbers do not appear in the paper. Prior correctly identified the study (CGIAR/IFPRI, Minya/Beni Suef). SINGLE-SOURCE flag: one study, two governorates in Upper Egypt, sample drawn from GIZ Agricultural Innovation Project database - not nationally representative. The MCIT/CAPMAS ICT Indicators Bulletin 2021-22 figure (rural household smartphone ownership 81% urban vs 68% rural) is quoted inside the same paper and offers the only quasi-national rural benchmark, but measures access, not literacy.
cells.protocol_issues: Indicator construct undefined: 'digital literacy among farmers (%)' has no standard measurement instrument in Egypt; available evidence measures barrier-shares (share citing illiteracy) and device/internet access. Recording as citation rather than gap because a real, well-sourced quantitative anchor exists; flag for Katreyna whether an inverse barrier-share may ever be scored against the H thresholds (recommend no).

cells.value: Government digital-extension channels are operating: El-Mufeed (FAO/MALR digital advisory app, launched 2020, content produced with ARC, presented to extension agents from all governorates) and Hudhud AI farmer assistant (MALR-MCIT, soft-launched 6 Dec 2021, described by MCIT as 'a paradigm shift in the agricultural guidance system'). Bundled advisory platforms including El-Mufeed, Mazra3ty and Fila7a reach tens of thousands of users (IFPRI, Dec 2025). The underlying public extension system is weak and its last full staffing observation is 2011: 7,421 public extension staff, of whom only 38 were ICT-support staff (IFPRI/FAO/IICA Worldwide Extension Study via GFRAS); ICARDA (2023) reports declining extension-officer numbers and that most farmers receive no agricultural advice.
cells.source_title: MCIT-MALR joint press release, 'Digital Transformation Services in Agriculture Announced' (6 December 2021)
cells.quality_evidence: Institutionalisation: FAO-MALR collaboration on El-Mufeed is formal - FAO converted ARC technical content to digital form and jointly rolled the app out to extension agents in all governorates (148 participants at the 22 Dec 2020 national rollout meeting; UN Egypt: https://egypt.un.org/en/106025-fao-malr-invite-extension-agents-use-%E2%80%9Cel-mufeed%E2%80%9D-app-and-disseminate-among-targeted-groups ; FAO Egypt app page: https://www.fao.org/egypt/our-office/the-fao-digital-app-of---el-mufeed-in-food-and-agriculture/en ). Digital extension is embedded in the joint MALR-MCIT program (T3, Dec 2021). Counter-evidence on system quality: ICARDA e-extension review (Attia & Govind 2023, https://cgspace.cgiar.org/items/36a7edda-f860-4a91-81df-c3fdc0e8ecec ) and ICARDA 'Current Situation of Digital Agriculture in Egypt' (Dec 2023, https://cgspace.cgiar.org/items/bbc4af9b-9c5b-42b4-8c95-997b40890722 ) report declining extension staffing, farmer knowledge gaps and uptake constraints (digital literacy, data-security concerns, platform maintenance costs).
cells.scale_evidence: IFPRI policy note (Abdallah, Abdelhadi & Karachiwalla, 'Digital Agricultural Technology in Egypt: Insights from App Developers', Dec 2025, T2): farm-management/advisory platforms incl. El-Mufeed 'reaching tens of thousands of users'; user bases range 'from 100K+ for Mahsoly and AlMorshed Poultry to 10K+ for several advisory platforms'; government-led apps (Al Mufeed, Hudhud, DAIRS) still face uptake constraints. No official MALR/MCIT count of extension agents actively using digital tools is published. Staffing denominator: 7,421 extension staff (2011 WWES via GFRAS, https://www.g-fras.org/en/world-wide-extension-study/africa/northern-africa/egypt.html - T4, page undated but data are 2011).
cells.search_trail: Searched 2026-08-22: T1 - FAO Egypt office pages (El-Mufeed presence confirmed; no reach numbers) -> T2 - CGSpace: ICARDA 2023 e-extension review, ICARDA Dec 2023 digital-agriculture situation report, IFPRI Dec 2025 app-developer policy note (PDF extracted and read) -> T3 - mcit.gov.eg press release 64824 and moa.gov.eg digital-transformation highlights page -> T4 - GFRAS worldwide extension study Egypt profile.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCES FROM PRIOR: (1) prior presented 7,421 extension staff as a current GFRAS figure; the GFRAS page reproduces 2011 Worldwide Extension Study data - staleness must be recorded (15 years). (2) Prior cited a 'GIZ Morshed Zaki pilot'; searched English and Arabic ('Morshed Zaki', 'المرشد الزكي') - no trace found in GIZ or any other source; treat as unverified, possibly fabricated. (3) Prior's 'ICARDA 2025 review' is actually an IFPRI policy note dated December 2025 that cites ICARDA 2023; the ICARDA situation report itself is dated 28 Dec 2023.
cells.protocol_issues: Single tier field is awkward for ladder cells whose presence facts are T3 and scale facts T2 - recorded as a compound tier string. GFRAS profile pages carry no on-page date for the underlying data (2011); this is a recurring staleness trap for extension indicators.

cells.value: A joint MALR-MCIT digital transformation program has been operating since 6 Dec 2021 (Hudhud AI assistant; agricultural e-portal with 20 services in trial operation; AI/satellite crop mapping; quarantine mechanisation; document archiving; Farmer Card: 3.5m+ printed, 2m distributed at launch). The MALR e-services portal is live (moa.gov.eg/our-services, checked 2026-08-22). However, no gazetted, named, staffed digital/AI unit inside MALR could be confirmed from T3 sources; MALR's published organisational units (e.g. Central Administration for Agricultural Planning, Central Administration for Agricultural Extension) do not include a digital-transformation administration. Long-standing AI capacity sits in ARC/MALR's Central Laboratory for Agricultural Expert Systems (CLAES, est. 1991 under an FAO/UNDP project).
cells.source_title: MCIT-MALR joint press release, 'Digital Transformation Services in Agriculture Announced' (6 December 2021)
cells.quality_evidence: Program-level institutionalisation is documented at T3: joint ministerial launch with named deliverables (MCIT PR 64824; MALR mirror page moa.gov.eg/highlights/خدمات-التحول-الرقمى); live e-services portal listing six service families incl. Digital Egypt inquiries and licensing (https://moa.gov.eg/our-services/ , checked 2026-08-22, site copyright 2026); the government 3-year plan 2024/2027 includes developing AI solutions in agriculture (SIS: https://sis.gov.eg/en/egypt/economy/pillars-of-the-economic-program/3-year-government-plan-20242027/ ). CLAES presence: GFAR directory listing (https://www.gfar.net/organizations/central-laboratory-agricultural-expert-systems-giza , T4) - the official ARC page (arc.sci.eg) was unreachable on the access date. UNIT-level evidence (name, staffing, budget of a digital unit inside MALR HQ) was NOT found at T3 - presence rung capped at Adopted for the indicator as defined, despite Operating-level evidence for the digital-transformation FUNCTION.
cells.scale_evidence: At launch (Dec 2021, T3): 3.5m+ Farmer Cards printed, 2m distributed; 20 e-services in trial operation. Lead (T5, NOT admissible as value): 2024-25 Egyptian press and ministerial statements claim ~3.2m agricultural holdings digitised against a 5.8m target (e.g. Dostor, Youm7) - route to initiative register for T3 confirmation.
cells.search_trail: Searched 2026-08-22: T1 - none applicable -> T2 - CGSpace/ICARDA/IFPRI Egypt digital-agriculture reports (no MALR unit named) -> T3 - moa.gov.eg (highlights, our-services, about pages), agri.gov.eg organisational pages, mcit.gov.eg press room, sis.gov.eg (3-year plan; September-2025 MALR-MCIT review cited by prior not located); Arabic searches for 'قطاع/إدارة مركزية/وحدة التحول الرقمي وزارة الزراعة' and ministerial decrees; arc.sci.eg CLAES page attempted (connection refused) -> T4 - GFAR/GFAiR CLAES listings.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCES FROM PRIOR: (1) prior's source for a 'MALR Digital Transformation Unit' was Zawya 2021 - a T5 news aggregator, inadmissible for indicator values under the protocol; the named unit could not be confirmed at any admissible tier in this pass. (2) The prior's 'Sept 2025 SIS review' of MALR-MCIT projects was searched for on sis.gov.eg but not located. (3) What IS verifiable at T3 is an operating joint PROGRAM and live services, plus CLAES as an institutionalised AI lab inside ARC since 1991 - a stronger and older institutional fact than the prior recorded.
cells.protocol_issues: Indicator ambiguity (DELIVERY flag): does an operating joint inter-ministerial program plus an ARC research lab satisfy 'a staffed, funded digital/AI unit inside MALR', or is a gazetted HQ unit required? Rung assignment depends on this definition - flagged for the defect log. Also: official ARC domain (arc.sci.eg) unreachable, forcing T4 fallback for CLAES.

cells.value: No dedicated agtech/digital-agriculture university degree or certificate program was identified for Egypt. Citable pipeline elements: (1) Digital Egypt Builders Initiative (DEBI, MCIT, launched Sept 2020 in the President's presence) - approx. 1,000 fully funded one-year master's scholarships per year in AI, data science, cybersecurity, robotics and related fields; general digital-talent pipeline, not agtech-specific. (2) AgriTech4Egypt Innovation Challenge (CGIAR Accelerate for Impact Platform with Alliance Bioversity-CIAT, ICARDA, IWMI, IFPRI and Egypt's Academy of Scientific Research and Technology; launched 27 Mar 2024) - fully funded 4-day Cairo bootcamp for 20 selected teams plus 5 CGIAR-led innovations, followed by a 6-month acceleration program with equity-free grants up to EGP 300,000; agtech-specific but a single documented cohort.
cells.source_title: MCIT, Digital Egypt Builders Initiative (DEBI) program page
cells.quality_evidence: DEBI is government-funded with an institutionalised annual cohort structure (1,000 scholarships/yr, international university partners, 100% tuition + stipend; T3 mcit.gov.eg). AgriTech4Egypt is backed by CGIAR A4IP and the Egyptian government's Academy of Scientific Research and Technology, funded by PRIMA, the Climate Resilient Africa Fund, ALEXBANK and the Syngenta Foundation (T2). The agtech-SPECIFIC pipeline is thin: one documented challenge cohort (2024), no evidence of recurrence found, and no university digital-agriculture/precision-agriculture degree located in searches of Egyptian faculties of agriculture (Cairo, Ain Shams, Mansoura).
cells.scale_evidence: DEBI: approx. 1,000 scholars/year since 2020 (T3). AgriTech4Egypt 2024: 20 teams + 5 CGIAR innovations in the bootcamp; launch event drew 100 participants from 52 countries (T2). No graduate-placement or agtech-employment statistics published for either.
cells.search_trail: Searched 2026-08-22: T1 - none applicable -> T2 - CGSpace/CGIAR (AgriTech4Egypt via Alliance Bioversity-CIAT); IFPRI Dec 2025 app-developer note (notes Egypt 'lags behind leaders like Morocco in agritech-specific incentives and incubator support') -> T3 - mcit.gov.eg DEBI page; university sites for 'precision agriculture'/'digital agriculture' programs (Cairo, Ain Shams, Mansoura faculties of agriculture - none found); Arabic search for university digital-agriculture programs -> T4 - Berytech AgriTech4Egypt program page (corroborating).
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE FROM PRIOR: prior recorded only 'Sector review - no dedicated program identified' (Announced/level-2 framing). Confirmed that no dedicated agtech degree exists, but the prior MISSED two citable pipeline elements: DEBI (T3, operating at scale since 2020, general data-science/AI) and AgriTech4Egypt (T2, agtech-specific bootcamp + acceleration, 2024). Presence rung 'Adopted' reflects: general digital-talent pipeline Operating, agtech-specific pipeline existent but not institutionalised as a recurring track.
cells.protocol_issues: Indicator definition ambiguity: does a general national data-science pipeline (DEBI) count toward an 'agtech/data-science training pipeline', or must programs be agtech-specific? Rung and any later level depend on this call - flagged for the defect log.

cells.value: DATA GAP — searched WDI/ILO female-agricultural-employment series and MCIT/CAPMAS ICT gender indicators (T1: population-level only, no digital-ag workforce breakdown); FAO Country Gender Assessment of the Agriculture and Rural Sector - Egypt (2022) and FAO Status of Women in Agrifood Systems (2023) (T2: no extension or digital-ag workforce gender share); moa.gov.eg / MALR publications (T3: nothing); GFRAS Worldwide Extension Study Egypt profile and JICA Egypt Country Gender Profile 2018 (T4: extension-staff proxies only, underlying data 2011). Searched 2026-08.
cells.source_title: JICA (2018). Country Gender Profile: Egypt - Table 3-11 'Number of Agricultural Extension Staff by Sex (2011)' (nearest proxy; not the indicator's construct)
cells.search_trail: Searched 2026-08-22 in tier order: T1 - WDI SL.AGR.EMPL.FE.ZS (female ag employment share - wrong construct), MCIT/CAPMAS ICT gender indicators (female internet use 65.2% - population-level) -> T2 - FAO CGA Egypt 2022 (women ~45% of official agricultural workforce; no extension/digital-workforce share), FAO Status of Women in Agrifood Systems 2023 -> T3 - moa.gov.eg, MALR publications: nothing -> T4 - GFRAS WWES Egypt profile (2011: women approx. 2% of field-level extension workers, 19% of subject-matter specialists, approx. 26% of senior management); JICA Egypt Country Gender Profile 2018 (PDF text-extracted and verified): 'the number of female extension staff members is extremely limited, with only 3.9 percent overall', Table 3-11, 2011 data compiled from the GFRAS website. No source measures the DIGITAL-agriculture workforce by gender.
cells.notes: DIVERGENCE FROM PRIOR: prior recorded 3.9 as a Measured value for this indicator (level 1). Verified that the 3.9% figure genuinely appears in JICA 2018 (Table 3-11) - but it measures women's share of ALL agricultural extension staff, using 2011 administrative data compiled from GFRAS, not the digital-agriculture workforce; and it is 15 years stale. Refuted as this indicator's value; recorded as gap with proxies preserved here. Related context: women are approx. 45% of Egypt's official agricultural workforce (FAO CGA 2022) and 65.2% of Egyptian women use the internet vs 79.3% of men (MCIT/CAPMAS) - neither is the indicator's construct.
cells.protocol_issues: Construct ambiguity: 'digital-ag workforce' is undefined (extension staff? agtech-company employees? ICT-in-agriculture roles?). The H 20/35/45/50 thresholds presuppose a measured share no Egyptian source publishes at any tier. If the ladder team decides extension staff count as digital-ag workforce, the 3.9%/2011 (JICA/GFRAS) figure could be promoted from proxy to stale value - flag for Katreyna.

bundle_issues: 1) STALENESS CLUSTER: the C4 people-and-institutions evidence base for Egypt rests heavily on 2011 Worldwide Extension Study data republished undated by GFRAS (extension staffing, ICT staff, female shares) - three of five cells touch it; any level-setting should treat these as 15-years stale. 2) PRIOR TIER HYGIENE: the v1.6 desk pass repeatedly used inadmissible or misdated sources in this bundle - Zawya (T5) as the sole basis for a 'MALR Digital Transformation Unit' (5.7); an 'ICARDA 2025 review' that is actually an IFPRI policy note of Dec 2025 citing ICARDA Dec 2023; a 'GIZ Morshed Zaki pilot' (5.5) that could not be found in English or Arabic and may be fabricated; and misquoted figures ('46-48%' vs the published 52%/54% in 5.4). 3) NO NATIONAL INSTRUMENT: CAPMAS/MCIT ICT surveys are household/individual-level and never farmer- or ag-workforce-disaggregated, so 5.4 and 5.12 cannot be closed from T1 as currently designed. 4) ACCESS FAILURES on 2026-08-22: arc.sci.eg (official ARC/CLAES page) connection-refused and en.enow.gov.eg PDF mirror reset - forced T4 fallbacks; icarda.org returned 403 on one training-news page. 5) ARCHIVING: protocol rule 3 requires Wayback captures for T4/T5 links at capture time; captures were not performed in this environment - flag for the capture step of the pipeline.
